errors.evidence: The description states there are seven “random layers” variants, but the chart shows five: “random layers,” “random layers +B₂,” “random layers +L₂,” “random layers +R₂,” and “random layers +permute”.

The description fails to mention the primary structural feature of the chart: that it is a grouped bar chart where each category on the x-axis has a pair of bars, one light-colored and one dark-colored. This omission makes subsequent value descriptions inaccurate or ambiguous.

errors.text_span: The “embedding” and “1st layer” bars (blue) show accuracies of approximately 80 and 82, respectively.
errors.evidence: This statement is ambiguous and inaccurate. There are four bars in these two categories combined (a light and dark bar for each). For “embedding,” the values are approx. 80 and 82. For “1st layer,” the values are approx. 81.5 and 82. The description conflates these four data points into two, without specifying which bar corresponds to which value.

errors.text_span: The “random layers” bars (green) are clustered around 80, with values ranging from approximately 79.5 to 81.
errors.evidence: This description obscures the two distinct data series. The light green bars are consistently at a lower value (approx. 79.5), while the dark green bars are consistently at a higher value (approx. 81.5). The stated range maximum of 81 is also incorrect as the dark bars are visibly higher.

errors.text_span: The “random” bars (red) are all clustered between approximately 71 and 73.
errors.evidence: This description over-generalizes the data by failing to distinguish between the two series of bars. The light red bars have values between approx. 71.5 and 72, while the dark red bars have values between approx. 73 and 73.5.
The taller of the two orange bars under the 'unperturbed' category has a value of approximately 91.5, not 92.
